newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy union leader says mini-budget wrong.
newsitem.headline: Italy union leader says mini-budget wrong.

text.p: The leader of Italy's largest trades union confederation on Wednesday called plans for a government mini-budget "incomprehensible and wrong".
"(This decision) is incomprehensible and wrong because it is a harbinger of possible social tensions," said Sergio Cofferati, head of the CGIL union confederation.
Cofferati said it would have been better if the government had waited for the trimester accounts due next month and "then tackle the real causes of the overshoot".

"If the objective of the government is to ensure stability of public accounts to get closer to the Maastricht parameters it would be good to bring forward the 1998 budget to before this summer," he said.
Cofferati was speaking to reporters after Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he had prepared the framework for a fresh budget.
Prodi said the cost-cutting mini-budget, to be launched in the coming weeks, would ensure Italy is a founder member of the single European currency. --Rome newsroom +396-6782501
